original_question: Let A be a sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity), and assume that -A generates a contractive C_0-semigroup. Must A then have a bounded H-infinity calculus, have bounded imaginary powers, or be R-analytic?
target_in_paper: The introductory open problem stated as Conjecture 1.1, together with its equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the positive partial result in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right ambient setting and the right phenomenon: an operator on an L^p-space with 1<p<∞, a contractive C_0-semigroup hypothesis, and the three regularity properties that the paper explicitly links together—bounded H^∞-calculus, bounded imaginary powers, and R-analyticity.
missing_details: The paper’s conjecture is about the analytic/sectorial angle < π/2 situation; saying only 'sectorial' is too weak unless one also specifies ω(A)<π/2, equivalently that -A generates a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup.
The semigroup hypothesis should be stated precisely as contractive on the real line, i.e. ||e^{-tA}||≤1 for all t≥0.

The target property in the conjecture is not three unrelated alternatives; the paper treats bounded H^∞-calculus as the main formulation, and Proposition 1.2 gives the equivalence with bounded imaginary powers and R-analyticity under the same contractive-semigroup hypothesis.
For the H^∞-calculus, the paper means a bounded H^∞(Σ_σ)-calculus for some angle σ<π/2.
For bounded imaginary powers, the paper’s intended strength is the angle < π/2 version, not merely pointwise boundedness of A^{it} with no angle/growth control.
R-analyticity should be phrased semigroup-theoretically: -A generates an R-analytic C_0-semigroup, equivalently A is R-sectorial of angle < π/2 in this setting.
To make the question stand alone, one should specify the ambient space as a complex L^p(Ω)-space and unpack the sectorial-operator convention used in the paper (closed, densely defined, dense range).

Theorem 1.3 is only a positive partial result: it adds positivity of the contractive semigroup. Your draft does not distinguish the conjectural general contractive case from this proven positive-contractivity case.
refined_question: Let 1<p<∞, let X=L^p(Ω) over the complex scalars, and let A be a closed densely defined operator with dense range on X such that A is sectorial of angle ω(A)<π/2 and -A generates a contractive C_0-semigroup (e^{-tA})_{t≥0} on X, i.e. ||e^{-tA}||≤1 for all t≥0. Must A then admit a bounded H^∞(Σ_σ)-functional calculus for some angle σ<π/2?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must -A generate an R-analytic C_0-semigroup (or, what is the same here by Proposition 1.2, must A have bounded imaginary powers of angle < π/2)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s introductory conjecture about whether contractivity of an analytic semigroup on an L^p-space forces the strongest regularity in the H^∞/BIP/R-analyticity chain. Conjecture 1.1 is the official formulation to target. Proposition 1.2 is exactly the nearby result that sharpens the wording by showing that, in this contractive-semigroup setting, bounded H^∞-calculus, bounded imaginary powers, and R-analyticity are equivalent formulations of the same question. Theorem 1.3 is the paper’s supporting positive result for the narrower case of positive contractive semigroups, so it should inform the context but not replace the conjecture.
